scope: NCERT national selected primary baseline: 12 formal Foundational stage records and 34 suggestive Grades 1–2 positions. Formal 3–8 stage window/stage-end and selected primary view remain separate; suggestive 6–8 does not invent per-grade cutoffs. No all-board claim.
coverageMeaning: Full is source-fit authoring coverage with explicit complete task/resource conditions, not actual learner attainment or automatic whole-topic mastery. Mixed records retain their contextual channels without compulsory liking, affection, comfort or emotional suppression.

records.rationale: Actual identity page and supplied/non-sensitive family/community relationships; explain their own membership, not just name an adult.
Recognise varied emotions and make a deliberate suitable response, with actual whole calming evidence kept separate from naming alone.
Actual responsive child/adult exchanges and appropriate help. Comfort is contextual and may coexist with reserve; performance is not inferred from mood.
records.contextualRequirement: Retained source affect/engagement channel; not a new binary mastery claim or a demand for positive feelings. Actual skill/action checks remain required.

Respond to another child’s different idea, preference and emotional need with an appropriate action; merely list differences is insufficient.
Complete genuinely useful age-appropriate school/home work with safety, shared responsibility and functional result.
Actual plant and animal engagement/care is checked; joy remains an observed/contextual channel rather than a compulsory feeling.

records.rationale: Follow the printed three-to-four ordered instructions/rules delivered together; actual four-step receipt, clarification and giving/checking instructions remain whole-card checks.
Child initiates a feasible actual shared activity, plans it and carries a useful contribution; leadership theory is not imposed.
Different partner/task cases include actual negotiation and fair distribution of responsibilities, not simply sit alongside another child.
Actual gentle handling/care appropriate to the life form; no harmful staged need or token animal-name response.
Actually germinate a locally suitable tree seed and tend its seedling with adult/species-specific care. Bean-only work cannot close the tree condition.
Actually identify local flora/fauna in their habitats and notice microhabitat conditions; curiosity/interest stays contextual.

records.rationale: Take a recurring actual plant/sapling-care responsibility using its checked care requirements; an observation diary alone does not prove care.
Respectful practical interaction with familiar/extended-family and neighbour roles; love is contextual and no private disclosure or prescribed family structure is required.
records.contextualRequirement: Retained source affect/engagement channel; not a new binary mastery claim or a demand for positive feelings. Actual skill/action checks remain required.

records.rationale: Actual appropriate verbal account. The printed stopping-crying example is not a universal no-tears condition; approved prompt correction makes the boundary explicit.
Actually adapt and perform a familiar story with an emotion conveyed, and make/tell a changed illustrated ending. Naming an emotion alone is insufficient.
Appropriate voluntary communication of an actual own feeling to a peer/familiar adult; fictional feeling vocabulary alone does not establish this duty.
Different safe social/physical contexts require an actual suitable flexible response; varied feelings remain legitimate. No manufactured upset or demanded instant calm.
Actual words conveying frustration and why, with non-harmful action; calm appearance or repeating an adult sentence is not enough.
Child initiates responsive peer exchanges in more than one familiar safe context; merely answer an adult-led prompt does not establish initiative.
Invent and carry out a feasible activity for at least two children, with meaningful roles and contributions; adult-given unknown/task cannot stand in for invention.
Both ask an appropriate person for needed help and provide useful practical help to another child; explanation alone does not prove either action.
Actually propose a play suggestion, listen to a peer proposal and follow the agreed feasible proposal, not always insist on their own.
Connect their actual friend relationship with a genuine helpful/inclusive example, while checking the complete qualities/near-miss claim separately. No forced friendship nomination.
Formulate respectful information-seeking questions about a supplied/voluntary profile, listen and use the answer. No compelled ethnicity, family or other private disclosure.
Recognise another child’s actual capability and explain something learned from them; general praise or comparison of worth is not the test.
Name a real same/different food/game preference and respond respectfully while the preference stays different; agreement is not required.
Use verified language-labelled supplied examples for the same referent; identify different labels without assuming English knowledge transfers to another language.

Reuse exact reviewed Ontario sibling claim: one person in different familiar roles, responsibilities and changing circumstances, with a new supplied transfer. Naming two labels alone is not whole-card success.

Coherent task and response to an actual difficulty, with changed approach and primary work planning. Increased attention uses stated comparable cases, not an invented universal duration.

Actual helpful, inclusive group actions remain assessable. Affection is contextual and never requires physical contact or a prescribed emotional display.

Take an appropriate recurring responsibility for an actual familiar animal under its responsible adult. Need knowledge/minibeast handling are components, not proof of dog/chicken/pet tending.
Actual accessible nature walk/observation with gentle care and habitat identification; joy is contextual and reserve does not erase observed skill.

before.subject: Personal & Social Development
before.name: Expressing Feelings with Words
before.description: Express their own feelings appropriately using words rather than actions — saying 'I feel angry because...' instead of hitting, shouting, or withdrawing
evidence: Use an 'I feel ___ when ___' statement during a disagreement
Choose to tell an adult how they feel instead of acting out physically
Describe their feelings about a difficult situation using at least two emotion words
before.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is frustrated — say a sibling takes their toy — do they use words to say how they feel rather than snatching it back or crying?

after.subject: Personal & Social Development
after.name: Expressing Feelings with Words
after.description: Express their own feelings appropriately using words rather than actions — saying 'I feel angry because...' instead of hitting, shouting, or withdrawing
evidence: Use an 'I feel ___ when ___' statement during a disagreement
Choose to tell an adult how they feel instead of acting out physically
Describe their feelings about a difficult situation using at least two emotion words
after.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is frustrated — say a sibling takes their toy — can they use words to say how they feel and why, rather than snatching it back or hurting someone? They may still feel upset or cry while explaining.

claimRevisions.wholeClaimWitness: A child says, while tearful, I feel sad and angry because you took the toy, tells an adult rather than hitting, and explains another difficult feeling using two appropriate emotion words. This demonstrates the full existing verbal-expression operation while failing the old no-crying prompt. Calm smiling silence or word repetition without communicating their own feeling does not demonstrate it.
claimRevisions.compatibility: Real assessment clarification affecting the continuing claim. Preserve old revision downstream; no automatic equivalence, transfer, reset or publication. No description/evidence/context/dependency edits proposed.

before.subject: Personal & Social Development
before.name: Taking Turns and Sharing
before.description: Take turns, share materials, and play cooperatively with others — understanding that group activities work better when everyone gets a fair go and that waiting for your turn is part of being a good friend
evidence: Take turns in a game or group activity without needing adult reminders
Share materials willingly during a shared task or playtime
Explain why taking turns makes games and group work more fun for everyone
before.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is playing a board game with friends or siblings, can they wait for their turn and share the pieces without grabbing or getting upset?

after.subject: Personal & Social Development
after.name: Taking Turns and Sharing
after.description: Take turns, share materials, and play cooperatively with others — understanding that group activities work better when everyone gets a fair go and that waiting for your turn is part of being a good friend
evidence: Take turns in a game or group activity without needing adult reminders
Share materials willingly during a shared task or playtime
Explain why taking turns makes games and group work more fun for everyone
after.assessmentPrompt: When {{name}} is playing a board game with friends or siblings, can they wait for their turn and share the pieces without grabbing or needing adult reminders, and explain why everyone getting a fair turn helps the game? They may still feel disappointed while doing so.

claimRevisions.wholeClaimWitness: A child disappointed about waiting nevertheless takes every turn without reminders, shares the pieces willingly, and explains why fair turns help everyone. Disappointment does not negate that whole operation; a smiling child who grabs or needs continual reminders fails.
claimRevisions.compatibility: Real assessment clarification affecting the continuing claim. Preserve old revision downstream; no automatic equivalence, transfer, reset or publication. No description/evidence/context/dependency edits proposed.

limits: Actual care/growing/local observation remains distinct from a model, need-list or positive attitude.
Species, life stage and local conditions qualify germination/habitat claims; no fixed tree-growth week, universal bee dependence or harmful animal deprivation is imported.
Read inherited guides with their recorded limits; historical source verification/confidence flags are not re-endorsed.
No forced touch, fearlessness, positive mood, private disclosure or staged distress is an assessment criterion.
Existing vocabulary/hard-path checks remain separately assessable current graph conditions, not extra universal NCERT language lists.
